data.note:
Specimen s_cedc34c90a unblinded as AZ-J (BBBC021 'Epithelial', no ChEMBL curated mechanism). My blinded call was Aurora kinase inhibitors (0.52, revised 0.61) and was scored incorrect.

Reflection: I over-weighted quantitative proxy features — frac_multinucleate_proxy z=7.9-10.9, frac_large_nucleus z~6, nuc_eccentricity z~7.5, nuc_solidity z negative — and the Microscopist's "multinucleation" description, interpreting them as cytokinesis failure. I under-weighted that (a) tub_mean was increased (z+3-4) with preserved tubulin/actin, (b) frac_mitotic_like never elevated (z ~0), rho 0.2 p0.8, inconsistent with Aurora/Eg5 mitotic arrest/slippage, and (c) both atlas comparisons (pooled e6 and 1µM clean-window e15) never returned Aurora/Eg5 neighbors — they consistently returned Protein synthesis (anisomycin, cycloheximide), Epithelial (PP-2, AZ-U), Cholesterol-lowering (simvastatin, mevinolin) with cosine 0.65-0.77, and at 1µM 4/10 Epithelial. The "multinucleation" was likely segmentation artifact from tight, round, solid colonies (cell_roundness z 4-7, solidity z 3.5-7, cell_area z -2.5 to -3.9) with closely apposed nuclei counted as one cell, not true multinucleation from Aurora inhibition. The dose response was also atypical for Aurora: monotonic nuc_area decrease rho -1.0 to z -6.3, but multinucleation proxy peaked at 1µM then fell at 10µM where cell loss appeared. I should have down-weighted Aurora after e6/e15 despite lack of high similarity, and kept Epithelial as top hypothesis.

Literature check: AZ-J has no curated mechanism and no directly returned PMID; searches for Aurora multinucleation and epithelial morphology screening returned no AZ-J-specific hits (generic epithelial morphology reviews e.g. PMID 28634961, 29525988, 40462136 were unrelated to AZ-J), consistent with reliance on atlas/phenotype. Future real-lab follow-up would be E-cadherin/β-catenin and p-EGFR/SFK pathway IF (PP-2/AZ-U controls) plus colony morphology assay, rather than phospho-H3S10/Aur

reflection.text:
Verdict was incorrect: I concluded Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.61 then p=0.52) while unblinding was AZ-J - truth Epithelial. The reflection is that I over-weighted a compelling nuclear phenotype and under-weighted the atlas, and then made a premature submit without using the cleanest window.

What the data did show correctly: There was a very strong apparent multinucleation signal. Well w_eefdd61b1d at 10 µM (503 cells) z=-8.8 nuc_major_axis, z=+8.0 frac_multinucleate_proxy (e2); w_0b5df1d0ab at 0.3 µM (285 cells) z=+9.0 frac_multinucleate_proxy (e3); w_443392cc3e at 1 µM (847 cells) z=+10.9 frac_multinucleate_proxy, z=+7.7 nuc_eccentricity (e8). Both microscopist calls (e4, e5, 4 fields and 2 fields, density lower vs DMSO) listed Aurora candidates. Dose-response checks correctly showed no mitotic arrest: frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.20 p=0.8 (e12), which argued against Eg5/microtubule stabilizer arrest, and tub_mean rho=+0.80 p=0.2 (e11) not supporting destabilizer. That part of the exclusion was right.

What misled me: I treated frac_multinucleate_proxy z>+8 as specific for Aurora/Eg5 cytokinesis failure. I discounted that segmentation of clustered epithelial cells, large eccentric nuclei (frac_large_nucleus z=+6.3 in e3, nuc_eccentricity ~+7.5-7.9 in e2/e3/e8) and lower cell density can inflate the same proxy. The very low-dose well w_033a39b2df at 0.03 µM (348 cells) already hinted at a non-mitotic morphology - act_tub_ratio z=+3.6, cell_eccentricity z=+2.1 (e7) - which is more consistent with actin/epithelial cytoskeletal remodeling than Aurora, but I logged it only as 'early onset' and did not update toward Epithelial.

What I missed in acquisition and comparison:

1. Atlas signal was contradictory from the start and I listed it as contradicting evidence instead of integrating it. First compare_to_reference_atlas (e6): Protein synthesis 5/10, Epithelial 3/10, Cholesterol-lowering 2/10 - Aurora 0/10. Hypothesis update at step 13 (e13) kept Aurora 0.61 with e6 merely as contradicting. That was confirmation bias toward the microscopist phrase and the large z-scores.

2. I chose a dose_response interpretation on only 4 wells that was underpowered. rho=+0.40 p=0.6 for frac_multinucleate_proxy (e9) is non-significant, yet I cited it as supporting Aurora. rho=-1.00 p=0 for nuc_area (e10) was taken as polyploidy vs shrinkage but is also expected with cell spreading/shape change. Non-significant p=0.6/0.2/0.8 trends should have been treated as inconclusive.

3. The critique is correct: the best potency window was never used for the decision. w_443392cc3e at 1 µM had the highest z=+10.9 *with no cell loss* (847 cells vs 503 cells at 10 µM and 285 at 0.3 µM) indicating toxicity/confounding at high dose diluting the dose trend, but I submitted (e14) before re-running the atlas on that profile. Even after the requested experiment, the second atlas (e15) on the 1 µM window was Epithelial 4/10, Protein synthesis 3/10, Cholesterol-lowering 2/10 - again Aurora 0/10 - and I still revised only to 0.52 Aurora (e16) and resubmitted (e17) with the same rationale.

Contributing factors: lookup_compound (e18) for AZ-J returned PubChem CID none, ChEMBL none, no curated mechanisms - BBBC021 internal code - so no chemical prior to correct me. search_literature for 'Aurora kinase inhibitor multinucleation cytokinesis failure MCF-7' returned 0 hits (e20), and the epithelial search (e21) returned no Aurora-supporting papers, so I had no literature backing. I did not have a PMID to cite for Aurora specificity, and the literature found in this run provided no direct support for the call, so I proceeded on phenotype alone.

Lesson: when a proxy nuclear feature is strong but atlas k=10 nearest neighbors consistently favor Epithelial/Protein synthesis and exclude the proposed MoA, and cell counts show a clean window (1 µM, 847 cells) distinct from toxic high dose, weight the atlas and the cell-count context over raw z-scores, and always run the atlas on the clean window before calling. My planned follow-up (phospho-H3S10/phospho-Aurora IF and live SiR-DNA) would have tested only Aurora vs Eg5 and would not have distinguished epithelial morphology - it should have included epithelial actin/cell-shape controls as the atlas suggested.
what_was_right: Strong statistical signal for enlarged/eccentric nuclei and high frac_multinucleate_proxy across e2/e3/e8 (z +8.0 to +10.9) and lower density vs DMSO (e4/e5) was real; exclusion of Eg5/microtubule arrest via e12 frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.20 p=0.8 and e11 tub_mean rho=+0.80 p=0.2 was correct direction.
what_was_wrong: Interpreted multinucleation proxy as Aurora-specific, ignoring that epithelial clustering/spreading inflates the same proxy; treated non-significant dose_response e9 rho=+0.40 p=0.6 as supportive; dismissed e6 and e15 atlas results (0/10 Aurora, Epithelial 3-4/10, Protein synthesis 3-5/10) as contradicting rather than primary evidence.
reflection.next_experiment: Re-ran atlas on already-acquired 1 µM profile (e15) and integrated e7 low-dose act_tub_ratio z=+3.6 / cell_eccentricity cytoskeletal hint; future: validate epithelial morphology with actin/E-cadherin IF and segmentation QC for cell clusters vs true multinucleation, versus Aurora/Eg5 references, not Aurora-only phospho-H3 assay.

1. Atlas signal was contradictory from the start and I listed it as contradicting evidence instead of integrating it. First compare_to_reference_atlas (e6): Protein synthesis 5/10, Epithelial 3/10, Cholesterol-lowering 2/10 - Aurora 0/10. Hypothesis update at step 13 (e13) kept Aurora 0.61 with e6 merely as contradicting. That was confirmation bias toward the microscopist phrase and the large z-scores.

2. I chose a dose_response interpretation on only 4 wells that was underpowered. rho=+0.40 p=0.6 for frac_multinucleate_proxy (e9) is non-significant, yet I cited it as supporting Aurora. rho=-1.00 p=0 for nuc_area (e10) was taken as polyploidy vs shrinkage but is also expected with cell spreading/shape change. Non-significant p=0.6/0.2/0.8 trends should have been treated as inconclusive.

3. The critique is correct: the best potency window was never used for the decision. w_443392cc3e at 1 µM had the highest z=+10.9 *with no cell loss* (847 cells vs 503 cells at 10 µM and 285 at 0.3 µM) indicating toxicity/confounding at high dose diluting the dose trend, but I submitted (e14) before re-running the atlas on that profile. Even after the requested experiment, the second atlas (e15) on the 1 µM window was Epithelial 4/10, Protein synthesis 3/10, Cholesterol-lowering 2/10 - again Aurora 0/10 - and I still revised only to 0.52 Aurora (e16) and resubmitted (e17) with the same rationale.

Contributing factors: lookup_compound (e18) for AZ-J returned PubChem CID none, ChEMBL none, no curated mechanisms - BBBC021 internal code - so no chemical prior to correct me. search_literature for 'Aurora kinase inhibitor multinucleation cytokinesis failure MCF-7' returned 0 hits (e20), and the epithelial search (e21) returned no Aurora-supporting papers, so I had no literature backing. I did not have a PMID to cite for Aurora specificity, and the literature found in this run provided no direct support for the call, so I proceeded on phenotype alone.

Lesson: when a proxy nuclear feature is strong but atlas k=10 nearest neighbors consistently favor Epithelial/Protein synthesis and exclude the proposed MoA, and cell counts show a clean window (1 µM, 847 cells) distinct from toxic high dose, weight the atlas and the cell-count context over raw z-scores, and always run the atlas on the clean window before calling. My planned follow-up (phospho-H3S10/phospho-Aurora IF and live SiR-DNA) would have tested only Aurora vs Eg5 and would not have distinguished epithelial morphology - it should have included epithelial actin/cell-shape controls as the atlas suggested.

What was right:
- Strong statistical signal for enlarged/eccentric nuclei and high frac_multinucleate_proxy across e2/e3/e8 (z +8.0 to +10.9) and lower density vs DMSO (e4/e5) was real; exclusion of Eg5/microtubule arrest via e12 frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.20 p=0.8 and e11 tub_mean rho=+0.80 p=0.2 was correct direction.

What was wrong or missed:
- Interpreted multinucleation proxy as Aurora-specific, ignoring that epithelial clustering/spreading inflates the same proxy; treated non-significant dose_response e9 rho=+0.40 p=0.6 as supportive; dismissed e6 and e15 atlas results (0/10 Aurora, Epithelial 3-4/10, Protein synthesis 3-5/10) as contradicting rather than primary evidence.

Proposed next experiment: Re-ran atlas on already-acquired 1 µM profile (e15) and integrated e7 low-dose act_tub_ratio z=+3.6 / cell_eccentricity cytoskeletal hint; future: validate epithelial morphology with actin/E-cadherin IF and segmentation QC for cell clusters vs true multinucleation, versus Aurora/Eg5 references, not Aurora-only phospho-H3 assay.
